statement.text: Let x_1x_2x_ denote the penalised minimiser over the constraint set; the identifier is written without spaces on purpose.
For every polynomial of degree at most 80 with coefficients bounded by one, f(x) = a_1 x + ... + a_80 x^80 <= C (1 + |x|)^p uniformly on the real line.
The tail sum R_m(x) vanishes as m tends to infinity, uniformly on compact sets.
The truncated expansion approximates f uniformly with an error of order 1/m.

Claim 1: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_1 = 9 and the remainder r_1(n) <= 1/n^2, so that <inequality 1> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument. Claim 2: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_2 = 3 and the remainder r_2(n) <= 2/n^2, so that <inequality 2> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument. Claim 3: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_3 = 10 and the remainder r_3(n) <= 3/n^2, so that <inequality 3> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument. Claim 4: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_4 = 4 and the remainder r_4(n) <= 4/n^2, so that <inequality 4> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument. Claim 5: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_5 = 11 and the remainder r_5(n) <= 5/n^2, so that <inequality 5> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument. Claim 6: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_6 = 5 and the remainder r_6(n) <= 6/n^2, so that <inequality 6> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument. Claim 7: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_7 = 12 and the remainder r_7(n) <= 7/n^2, so that <inequality 7> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument. Claim 8: for every n >= n_0 and every delta in (0, 1), the estimator theta_hat(n, delta) satisfies the oracle inequality with constant C_8 = 6 and the remainder r_8(n) <= 8/n^2, so that <inequality 8> holds with probability at least 1 - delta & the union bound closes the argument.
